    33	/-- Applying the canonical line-representative projection twice has the same
    34	effect as applying it once. This is the fixed-point fact used by the tagged
    35	carrier below. -/
    36	theorem lineRepMap_apply_self {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    37	    (v u : Fin m → K) :
    38	    lineRepMap v (lineRepMap v u) = lineRepMap v u := by
    39	  simp [lineRepMap, canonicalProjOfKernel, LinearMap.comp_apply]
    40	
    41	/-- The two presentations of lines used by the low-degree question sampler. -/
    42	inductive LineKind where
    43	  | axis
    44	  | diagonal
    45	  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
    46	
    47	/-- The tagged canonical carrier of `def:line-point-dist`, blueprint
    48	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:81-90`, paper
    49	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:174-186`.
    50	
    51	An axis description stores its canonical base and seed. A diagonal description
    52	stores only the projected direction, together with its prefix-zero invariant.
    53	Both constructors carry the assertion that their base is fixed by the
    54	appropriate `lineRepMap`. -/
    55	inductive LineDesc (L : LdParams) where
    56	  | axis (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    57	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)) base = base)
    58	  | diagonal (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    59	      (direction : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
    60	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
    61	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L seed).val → direction j = 0)
    62	  deriving DecidableEq
    63	
    64	/-- The tag of a canonical line description. -/
    65	def LineDesc.kind {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → LineKind
    66	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
    67	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
    68	
    69	/-- The seed retained by a canonical line description. -/
    70	def LineDesc.seed {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → ScalarQ L
    71	  | .axis _ seed _ => seed
    72	  | .diagonal _ seed _ _ _ => seed
    73	
    74	/-- The canonical base stored by a line description. -/
    75	def LineDesc.base {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → Fin L.m → ScalarQ L
    76	  | .axis base _ _ => base
    77	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
    78	
    79	/-- The geometric direction represented by a canonical line description.
    80	Diagonal constructors already store the projected data, so this accessor does
    81	not apply a second projection. -/
    82	def LineDesc.direction {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    83	    Fin L.m → ScalarQ L :=
    84	  match line with
    85	  | .axis _ seed _ => coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)
    86	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction
    87	
    88	/-- The canonical base is fixed by the representative map of the line's
    89	geometric direction. -/
    90	theorem LineDesc.base_fixed {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    91	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
    92	  cases line with
    93	  | axis base seed baseFixed => exact baseFixed
    94	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
    95	
    96	/-- Every diagonal description carries the source prefix-zero invariant. -/
    97	theorem LineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L)
    98	    (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
    99	    ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L line.seed).val → line.direction j = 0 := by
   100	  cases line with
   101	  | axis base seed baseFixed => simp [LineDesc.kind] at hline
   102	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
   103	
   104	/-- The point set represented by a seed-bearing line description. -/
   105	noncomputable def LineDesc.pointSet {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
   106	    Set (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :=
   107	  linePoints line.base line.direction
   108	
   109	/-- Coefficient-list representation of a univariate polynomial of degree at
   110	most `c` over the scalar field of `L`. -/
   111	abbrev DegPoly (L : LdParams) (c : ℕ) := Fin (c + 1) → ScalarQ L
   112	
   113	/-- Evaluate a bounded coefficient-list polynomial. -/
   114	def degPolyEval {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ}
   115	    (f : DegPoly L c) (t : ScalarQ L) : ScalarQ L :=
   116	  ∑ i : Fin (c + 1), f i * t ^ i.val
   117	
   118	/-- Extend a coefficient list by zero from degree bound `c` to `c'`. -/
   119	def DegPoly.padTo {L : LdParams} {c c' : ℕ} (_h : c ≤ c')
   120	    (f : DegPoly L c) : DegPoly L c' :=
   121	  fun i =>
   122	    if hi : i.val < c + 1 then f ⟨i.val, hi⟩ else 0
   123	
   124	/-- A line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` has a line parameter
   125	and every such parameter gives the same value.  The universal clause handles
   126	the zero-direction presentation without choosing a sentinel parameter. -/
   127	def EvaluatesTo {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   128	    (f : DegPoly L c) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (a : ScalarQ L) : Prop :=
   129	  (∃ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
   130	    ∀ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction → degPolyEval f t = a
   131	
   132	/-- Evaluate a line polynomial at a point, returning `none` precisely when the
   133	point does not determine an evaluation.  The `Option` completion is the
   134	paper's bottom outcome for malformed or nonincident answers. -/
   135	noncomputable def evalOpt {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   136	    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (f : DegPoly L c) : Option (ScalarQ L) := by
   137	  classical
   138	  exact if h : ∃ a : ScalarQ L, EvaluatesTo line f u a then
   139	    some (Classical.choose h)
   140	  else none

   142	/-- Convert an axis-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation. -/
   143	def aLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   144	  let direction := coordinateDirection (chiIndex L line.seed)
   145	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   146	  LineDesc.axis base line.seed (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point)
   147	
   148	/-- Convert a diagonal-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation. -/
   149	def dLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   150	  let direction := prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction
   151	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   152	  LineDesc.diagonal base line.seed direction
   153	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point) (by
   154	      intro j hj
   155	      change prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction j = 0
   156	      rw [prefixProjection, if_pos hj])
   157	
   158	/-- The affine-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler. -/
   159	noncomputable def aLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   160	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   161	  (clDistribution (ldALineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   162	    (aLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   163	
   164	/-- The diagonal-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler. -/
   165	noncomputable def dLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   166	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   167	  (clDistribution (ldDLineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>

   169	
   170	/-- The equal mixture of affine and diagonal line-point samples.  The
   171	parameter record is explicit, so the same definition works at every dimension. -/
   172	noncomputable def linePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   173	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   174	  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   175	    (aLinePointDist L) (dLinePointDist L)
   176	
   177	/-- The affine line-point component has total probability one. -/
   178	theorem aLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   179	    (aLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   180	  sorry
   181	
   182	/-- The diagonal line-point component has total probability one. -/
   183	theorem dLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   184	    (dLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   185	  sorry
   186	
   187	/-- The line-point mixture has total probability one. -/
   188	theorem linePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   189	    (linePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   190	  exact Distribution.mix_isProbability _ _ _
   191	    (aLinePointDist_isProbability L) (dLinePointDist_isProbability L)
   192	    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)

     4	/-!
     5	# Games, tensor-product strategies, and value
     6	
     7	This file provides the finite game carrier used by the Pauli basis test.  Pure
     8	states are vectors in `EuclideanSpace`, and POVMs use the project's matrix
     9	`Measurement` structure.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The source-facing nodes are `def:game`, `def:povm-conventions`,
    14	`def:tensor-product-strategy`, and `def:tensor-product-value` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:47-82` and `8-26`.
    16	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-57`.
    17	-/

    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	/--
    27	A finite two-player one-round game with a probability distribution on question
    28	pairs and a Boolean decision predicate.  This is `def:game` in
    29	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:51-59`, with paper origin
    30	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-24`.

    32	structure Game where
    33	  QuestionA : Type
    34	  QuestionB : Type
    35	  AnswerA : Type
    36	  AnswerB : Type
    37	  [questionAFintype : Fintype QuestionA]
    38	  [questionBFintype : Fintype QuestionB]
    39	  [answerAFintype : Fintype AnswerA]
    40	  [answerBFintype : Fintype AnswerB]
    41	  [questionADecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionA]
    42	  [questionBDecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionB]
    43	  [answerADecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerA]
    44	  [answerBDecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerB]

    46	  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
    47	  decide : QuestionA → QuestionB → AnswerA → AnswerB → Bool

    49	attribute [instance] Game.questionAFintype Game.questionBFintype
    50	  Game.answerAFintype Game.answerBFintype Game.questionADecidableEq
    51	  Game.questionBDecidableEq Game.answerADecidableEq Game.answerBDecidableEq
    52	
    53	/--
    54	The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This
    55	is the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation

    61	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    62	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    63	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=

    71	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    72	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    73	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement β d :=

    84	The tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in

    88	structure Strategy (G : Game) where
    89	  ιA : Type
    90	  ιB : Type
    91	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
    92	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
    93	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
    94	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
    95	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
    96	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    97	  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
    98	  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB
    99	
   100	attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
   101	  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq
   102	
   103	/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
   104	the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
   107	-/
   108	def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
   109	  Matrix.kronecker A B
   110	
   111	/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
   112	functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
   113	using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
   114	/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
   115	action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   117	noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   118	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
   119	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ
   120	
   121	/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
   122	`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   124	private noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   125	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   126	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   127	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
   128	  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
   129	  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re
   130	
   131	/--
   132	The tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born
   133	probabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in
   134	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin
   135	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.
   136	-/
   137	noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=
   138	  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>
   139	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   140	      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)
   141	
   142	/--
   143	The tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite
   144	strategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested
   145	for `def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint
   146	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper origin
   147	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`; attainment is
   148	intentionally not asserted here.
   149	-/
   150	noncomputable def Game.value (G : Game) : ℝ :=
   151	  sSup (Set.range (fun S : Strategy G => S.value))
   152

1	# Mathematical Language Guidelines
     2	
     3	MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
     4	the formalization with the paper and blueprint.
     5	
     6	This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
     7	naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
     8	`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.
     9	
    10	## Scope
    11	
    12	These guidelines apply to:
    13	
    14	- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
    15	- module docstrings;
    16	- declaration docstrings;
    17	- documentation-visible section comments;
    18	- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
    19	- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
    20	- issue titles and issue bodies;
    21	- PR titles and PR descriptions.
    22	
    23	## Source of Truth
    24	
    25	Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:
    26	
    27	1. `references/ldt-paper/`
    28	2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
    29	3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files
    30	
    31	When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
    32	example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
    33	projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.
    34	
    35	## Reference Notation And Terminology
    36	
    37	The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
    38	reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
    39	docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
    40	without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.
    41	
    42	When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
    43	location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
    44	first applicable location in the following order:
    45	
    46	1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
    47	   differs from the paper;
    48	2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
    49	   family of declarations in that file;
    50	3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
    51	   blueprint;
    52	4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
    53	   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.
    54	
    55	The explanation should say:
    56	
    57	- the notation or term used in the paper;
    58	- the Lean object or name which represents it;
    59	- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
    60	- the scope in which the replacement should be used.
    61	
    62	A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
    63	where future readers can learn it.
    64	
    65	Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
    66	should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
    67	rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.
    68	
    69	## Naming Norm
    70	
    71	Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
    72	conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
    73	assembled.
    74	
    75	Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
    76	`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
    77	uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
    78	such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
    79	clearer phrase.
    80	
    81	This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
    82	Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
    83	blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
    84	mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
    85	number, or implementation history.
    86	
    87	### Concrete examples
    88	
    89	The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
    90	codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
    91	others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
    92	process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
    93	assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
    94	paper or blueprint would recognize.
    95	
    96	| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
    97	|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
    98	| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
    99	| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
   100	| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
   101	| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
   102	| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
   103	| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
   104	| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
   105	| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
   106	| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
   107	| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |
   108	
   109	An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
   110	phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
   111	In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.
   112	
   113	File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
   114	named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
   115	exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.
   116	
   117	### Shared helpers
   118	
   119	When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
   120	more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
   121	shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
   122	ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
   123	call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.
   124	
   125	Procedure:
   126	
   127	1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   128	   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   129	   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   130	   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   131	   explicit argument.
   132	2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   133	   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   134	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   135	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   136	   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
   137	3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   138	   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
   139	4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   140	   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   141	   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   142	   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   143	   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   144	   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
   145	5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   146	   blueprint location it supports.
   147	
   148	### Legacy identifier treatment
   149	
   150	If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
   151	describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
   152	identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
   153	in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.
   154	
   155	Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   156	public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
   157	shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
   158	blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.
   159	
   160	## Review Checklist
   161	
   162	Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
   163	documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.
   164	
   165	- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
   166	      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
   167	      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
   168	      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
   169	      implementation-phase labels)?
   170	- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
   171	      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
   172	      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
   173	      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
   174	      source does not use them that way?
   175	- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
   176	      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
   177	      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
   178	      that order of preference?
   179	- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
   180	      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
   181	      construction they support?
   182	- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
   183	      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
   184	      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
   185	- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
   186	      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
   187	      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
   188	      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
   189	- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
   190	      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
   191	      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
   192	      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.
   193	
   194	Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
   195	relevant audit before changing names or prose.
   196

    68	\begin{definition}[Complementary subspaces]\label{def:complementary}
    69		Two subspaces $S$ and $T$ of a linear space $V$ form a pair of
    70		\emph{complementary subspaces} of $V$ if
    71		\[

    73		\]

    75		uniquely as $x = x^S + x^T$ with $x^S \in S$ and $x^T \in T$; we call $x^S$
    76		(resp.\ $x^T$) the \emph{projection of $x$ onto $S$ parallel to $T$} (resp.\
    77		onto $T$ parallel to $S$). The unique linear map $L : V \to V$ with
    78		$x \mapsto x^S$ is the \emph{projector onto $S$ parallel to $T$}.
    79	\end{definition}

    81	A subspace may have many complementary subspaces: in $\F_2^2$, the subspace
    82	$S = \mathrm{span}\{(1,1)\}$ has the distinct complements
    83	$\mathrm{span}\{(1,0)\}$ and $\mathrm{span}\{(0,1)\}$. Given a basis of $S$,
    84	one may nevertheless single out a \emph{canonical} complement.

    86	\begin{definition}[Canonical complement]\label{def:canonical-complement}
    87		\uses{def:register-subspace}
    88		Let $\hat{E}$ be the standard basis of $V = \F^n$ and let
    89		$F = \{v_1, \dots, v_m\} \subset V$ be a set of $m$ linearly independent
    90		vectors. Write $v_i = \sum_{j=1}^n a_{i,j}\, \hat{e}_j$, and, using a
    91		canonical Gaussian-elimination algorithm valid over arbitrary fields,
    92		transform the $m \times n$ matrix $(a_{i,j})$ to reduced row echelon form
    93		$(b_{i,j})$. Let $J$ be the set of $m$ column indices containing the leading
    94		$1$ entry of each row of $(b_{i,j})$. The \emph{canonical complement of $F$}
    95		is the set of $n - m$ standard basis vectors
    96		\[
    97			F^\perp = \{\hat{e}_j : j \notin J\}\;.
    98		\]
    99		The canonical complement is a \emph{set} of vectors, not a subspace.
   100		% Basis-independence made explicit here: the source defines F^perp through
   101		% a basis but does not assert dependence on it; uniqueness of the reduced
   102		% row echelon form gives dependence on span(F) alone.
   103		Although defined through the basis $F$, it depends only on
   104		$\mathrm{span}(F)$ and the ambient standard basis: two bases of the same
   105		subspace form the rows of row-equivalent matrices, which have the same
   106		reduced row echelon form and hence the same pivot set $J$. The presentation
   107		through Gaussian elimination, adopted by \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}, makes the
   108		canonical complement efficiently computable. If $S$ is a register subspace
   109		spanned by $\hat{E}_0 \subseteq \hat{E}$, then the canonical complement of
   110		$\hat{E}_0$ is $\hat{E} \setminus \hat{E}_0$, and its span coincides with
   111		$S^\perp$.
   112	\end{definition}

   114	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:canonical-complement}
   115		\uses{def:canonical-complement, def:complementary}
   116		Let $S$ be the span of linearly independent vectors
   117		$F = \{v_1, \dots, v_m\} \subseteq V$, let $F^\perp$ be the canonical
   118		complement of $F$, and let $T = \mathrm{span}(F^\perp)$. Then
   119		\[
   120			S + T = V\;, \qquad S \cap T = \{0\}\;.
   121		\]
   122	\end{lemma}
   123	\begin{proof}
   124		\uses{def:canonical-complement}
   125		Let $A = (a_{i,j})$ be the $m \times n$ matrix whose rows are the $v_i$ and
   126		write $A = UB$ with $U$ invertible and $B$ in reduced row echelon form, so
   127		that the rows of $B$ are linearly independent and span $S$. The restrictions
   128		of the rows of $B$ to the columns in $J$ are still linearly independent and
   129		span $\F^m$, so for every $u \in V$ there is $v \in S$ that agrees with $u$
   130		on the coordinates in $J$. The difference $u - v$ is then supported on the
   131		coordinates outside $J$, that is, $u - v \in T$, which proves $S + T = V$.
   132		Counting dimensions forces $S \cap T = \{0\}$.
   133	\end{proof}

   139		$L \in \mathrm{End}(V)$ with kernel basis $F$} is the projector onto $T$
   140		parallel to $S$, where $S = \mathrm{span}(F)$ and
   141		$T = \mathrm{span}(F^\perp)$; this is well defined by
   142		Lemma~\ref{lem:canonical-complement}. Since the canonical complement
   143		depends only on $\mathrm{span}(F)$
   144		(Definition~\ref{def:canonical-complement}), so does $L$, and we also call
   145		it the \emph{canonical linear map with kernel $S$}. Note that
   146		$\ker(L) = S$.

   335	\begin{definition}[Individual and total degree]\label{def:polynomials-degree}
   336		\uses{def:polyfunc}
   337		An $m$-variate polynomial $f$ over $\F_q$ is a function of the form
   338		\[
   339			f(x_1, \dots, x_m) = \sum_{\alpha \in \{0, 1, \dots, q-1\}^m}
   340			c_\alpha\, x_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots x_m^{\alpha_m}
   390		individual-degree form.
   391	\end{remark}
   392	
   393	The Schwartz--Zippel lemma implies that low-degree polynomials form an
   394	error-correcting code with good distance, the \emph{low-degree code} (a special
   395	case of the generalized Reed--Muller code).
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree encoding]\label{def:low-degree-encoding}
   398		\uses{def:polynomials-degree}
   399		Fix an integer $m \in \N$ and let $M = 2^m$. For every $y \in \{0,1\}^m$
   400		define the $m$-variate multilinear polynomial over $\F_q$
   401		\[
   402			\mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(x)
   403			= \prod_{i : y_i = 1} x_i \cdot \prod_{i : y_i = 0} (1 - x_i)\;,
   404		\]
   405		identifying $\{0,1\}$ with a subset of $\F_q$. Restricted to the subcube
   406		$\{0,1\}^m$, the polynomial $\mathrm{ind}_{m,y}$ vanishes everywhere except
   407		at $x = y$, where it equals $1$. For $a \in \F_q^M$, label the coordinates
   408		of $a$ as $a_y$ for $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ (identifying $\{0,1\}^m$ with
   409		$\{1, \dots, M\}$ by the lexicographic ordering). The \emph{low-degree
   410		encoding of $a$} is the multilinear polynomial $g_a : \F_q^m \to \F_q$,
   411		% Paper equation label kept on the display it names.
   412		\begin{equation}\label{eq:ld-encoding}
   413			g_a(x) = \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} a_y \cdot \mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(x)\;.
   414		\end{equation}
   415		For every $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ one has $g_a(y) = a_y$, and $g_a$ has total
   416		degree at most $m$.
   417	\end{definition}
   418	
   419	\begin{definition}[Indicator vector and linearity of the encoding]\label{def:indicator-vector}
   420		\uses{def:low-degree-encoding, def:dot-product-orthogonal}
   421		For $x \in \F_q^m$, the \emph{indicator vector} is
   422		\[
   423			\mathrm{ind}_m(x)
   424			= \bigl(\mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(x)\bigr)_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} \in \F_q^M\;.
   425		\]
   426		With this notation the low-degree encoding satisfies, for every
   427		$a \in \F_q^M$ and $x \in \F_q^m$,
   428		% Paper equation label kept on the display it names.
   429		\begin{equation}\label{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}
   430			g_a(x) = a \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(x)\;;
   431		\end{equation}
   432		in particular the map $a \mapsto g_a$ is $\F_q$-linear.
   433	\end{definition}
   434	
   435	Since encodings $g_a$ are multilinear, hence of total degree at most $m$, two
   436	encodings of distinct strings agree on at most an $m/q$ fraction of points of
   437	$\F_q^m$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel}.

    12	construction theorem.

    14	## References

    17	`def:dot-product-orthogonal`, `def:canonical-complement`, and
    18	`def:cl-canonical` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex`;

    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

    26	variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

    28	/--

    30	by `S`.  It is the Lean encoding of `def:register-subspace` from
    31	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:24-29`, whose paper origin is
    32	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:231-239`.

    34	def registerSubmodule (K : Type*) [Field K] (S : Finset ι) : Submodule K (ι → K) :=

    36	
    37	/--
    38	`dotOrthogonal W` consists of vectors whose coordinate dot product with every
    39	member of `W` vanishes.  This is `def:dot-product-orthogonal` in
    40	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:31-42`, with paper origin
    41	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:241-255`.

    43	def dotOrthogonal (W : Submodule K (ι → K)) : Submodule K (ι → K) where
    44	  carrier := {u | ∀ v, v ∈ W → dotProduct u v = 0}
    45	  zero_mem' := by
    46	    intro v hv
    47	    simp [dotProduct]
    48	  add_mem' := by
    49	    intro u v hu hv w hw
    50	    calc
    51	      dotProduct (u + v) w =
    52	          (dotProduct u w) + (dotProduct v w) := by
    53	            change (∑ i, (u i + v i) * w i) =
    54	              (∑ i, u i * w i) + (∑ i, v i * w i)
    55	            simp_rw [add_mul]
    56	            rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    57	      _ = 0 := by rw [hu w hw, hv w hw, add_zero]
    58	  smul_mem' := by
    59	    intro c u hu v hv
    60	    calc
    61	      dotProduct (c • u) v = c * dotProduct u v := by
    62	        simp [dotProduct, smul_eq_mul, mul_assoc, Finset.mul_sum]
    63	      _ = 0 := by rw [hu v hv, mul_zero]
    64	
    65	/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to the first `k` coordinates.  Lean-only rank
    66	infrastructure for `def:canonical-complement`, blueprint
    67	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:84-110`, paper `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:231-384`.
    68	-/
    69	private def prefixMap (k n : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n) :
    70	    (Fin n → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin k → K) :=
    71	  { toFun := fun x i => x ⟨i.1, lt_of_lt_of_le i.2 hk⟩
    72	    map_add' := by
    73	      intro x y
    74	      rfl
    75	    map_smul' := by
    76	      intro c x
    77	      rfl }

    79	/-- The rank of a prefix restriction used by the pivot characterization. -/
    80	private noncomputable def prefixRank {n : ℕ} (W : Submodule K (Fin n → K))
    81	    (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n) : ℕ :=
    82	  Module.finrank K (W.map (prefixMap k n hk))
    83	
    84	/--
    85	The non-pivot coordinate set of `W`, defined by the rank-increase
    86	characterization of pivots.  This is the basis-free encoding approved for
    87	`def:canonical-complement` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:84-110`;
    88	the paper's Gaussian-elimination presentation is
    89	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:303-320`.
    90	-/
    91	noncomputable def canonicalComplement {n : ℕ}
    92	    (W : Submodule K (Fin n → K)) : Finset (Fin n) :=
    93	  Finset.univ.filter fun j =>

   105	    (W : Submodule K (Fin n → K)) :

   108	
   109	/--
   110	The projector onto the canonical coordinate complement along `W`.  This is
   111	`def:cl-canonical` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:133-145`,
   112	originating at `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:375-384`.
   113	-/
   114	noncomputable def canonicalProjOfKernel {n : ℕ}
   115	    (W : Submodule K (Fin n → K)) : (Fin n → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin n → K) := by

   188		Let $\{\ket{\psi_n}\}_{n \in \N}$ and $\{\ket{\psi'_n}\}_{n \in \N}$ be two families of states in the same space $\mathcal H$. For a function $\delta \colon \N \to [0,1]$ we say that $\{\ket{\psi_n}\}$ and $\{\ket{\psi'_n}\}$ are \emph{$\delta$-close}, denoted $\ket{\psi} \approx_\delta \ket{\psi'}$, if
   189		\[
   190			\lVert \ket{\psi_n} - \ket{\psi'_n} \rVert^2 = O(\delta(n))\,.
   191		\]

   117	  
   118	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{axis-parallel} if there is a coordinate $i \in
   119	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ for which $v$ is equal to $e_i$, the $i$-th elementary basis
   120	  vector in $\F_q^m$.
   121	  We say that such a line $\line$ is \emph{parallel to the $i$-th direction}.
   122	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{diagonal} if there exists an $i \in
   123	  \{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$ for which $v_1 = v_2 = \cdots = v_i = 0$.
   124	\end{definition}
   125	
   126	The following Proposition establishes that, for a fixed direction, a line
   127	$\line$ is an equivalence class of points on the line.
   128	\begin{proposition}
   129	  \label{prop:line-equiv}
   130	  Let $u,v \in \F_q^m$.
   131	  Then for all $u' \in \line(u,v)$, we have that $\line(u,v) = \line(u',v)$.
   132	\end{proposition}
   133	\begin{proof}
   134		Fix $u' \in \line(u,v)$.
   135	  We have that $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$.
   136	  Let $a \in \line(u,v)$.
   137	  This means that $a = u + sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$.
   138	  We also have that $a = u + (s - t + t)v = u + tv + (s - t)v = u' + (s - t)v$,
   139	  so $\line(u,v) \subseteq \line(u',v)$.
   140	  A similar argument shows that $\line(u',v) \subseteq \line(u,v)$.
   141	\end{proof}
   142	
   143	We now specify a canonical representation of lines $\line = \line(u,v)$ as pairs $(u_0,v)$
   144	where $u_0$ is a \emph{canonical representative} of $\line$ specified as
   145	follows.
   146	Let $L_v^{\lnf}: \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with the
   147	one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$ (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical} for a
   148	definition of canonical linear map).
   149	Note that for all $u \in \line$, we have that $L_v^{\lnf}(u)$ is a point in
   150	$\line$.
   151	This is because since the image and kernel of $L_v^{\lnf}$ are complementary
   152	subspaces by definition (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical}), any $u \in \F_q^m$ has a
   153	unique decomposition $u = u_0 + u_1$ where $u_0$ is in the image of $L_v^{\lnf}$
   154	and $u_1 \in \ker(L_v^{\lnf})$, which by definition is the subspace spanned by
   155	$v$.
   156	Thus $u_1 = tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$ and we have that $u_0 = u - tv \in \line$.
   157	In particular, if $u\in \line$ then $u_0 = L_v^{\lnf}(u) \in \line$ as well. 
   158	Furthermore, since $L_v^{\lnf}$ is a projection onto its image by definition, we
   159	have $L_v^{\lnf}(u_0) = u_0$.
   160	
   161	Next, note that for any $u,u' \in \line$, since $u-u' = sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$
   162	it follows that $L_v^\lnf(u) = L_v^\lnf(u')$.
   163	Thus $u_0 = u_0'$ and this shows that $L_v^\lnf$ gives a means to compute a
   164	canonical representative of lines.
   165	
   166	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]
   167	  \label{def:line-representative}
   168	  Let $\line$ be a line in direction $v$.
   169	  A canonical representative of $\line$ is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   170	  \[
   171	    u_0 = L_v^\lnf(u)
   172	  \]
   173	  for all $u \in \line$.
   174	\end{definition}

   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for

  1238	  The state is
  1239	  \begin{equation*}

  1244	  $\ALine$, $\DLine$, and $\Pauli$.

  1246	  Z\}$,
  1247	  \begin{align*}
  1248	    E^{(\Point,W),\, y}_{\, a}
  1249	    & = \tau^W_{[g_{\cdot}(y) = a]} \otimes I\;,\\

  1251	    & = \tau^W_{[(g_{\cdot})|_\line = f]} \otimes I\;,\\
  1252	    E^{(\DLine,W),\, \line}_{\, f}
  1253	    & = \tau^W_{[(g_{\cdot})|_\line = f]} \otimes I\;,\\

  1255	    & = \tau^W_{a} \otimes I\;.
  1256	  \end{align*}

  1258	  defined in \Cref{def:bracket}.
  1259	  Thus, for example, the measurement on question $((\Point,W),y)$ corresponds to
  1260	  first performing the measurement $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^M}$, receiving an
  1261	  outcome $h \in \F_q^M$, and then outputting the value $a = g_{h}(y)$.
  1262	
  1263	  For $\ALine$ and $\DLine$ questions, the question content $\line$ denotes
  1264	  either an axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$ for some $i \in
  1265	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$, or a diagonal line $\line(u_0,v')$ for some $v' \in
  1266	  \F_q^m$.
  1267	  As described at the beginning of \Cref{sec:qld-game}, axis-parallel lines are
  1268	  specified by pairs $(u_0,s) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q$ and diagonal lines are
  1269	  specified by triples $(u_0,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times \F_q^m$.
  1270	  The measurement on question $((\ALine,W),\line)$, for example, corresponds to
  1271	  first performing the measurement $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^M}$ to get an
  1272	  outcome $h \in \F_q^M$, and reporting the univariate polynomial $f_\line(t) =
  1273	  g_{h}(u_0 + te_i)$ where $\line$ is specified by $(u_0,s)$ and $i = \chi(s)$.
  1274	  
  1275	
  1276	
  1277	  Next we specify the POVMs associated with questions of type $\Constraint$,
  1278	  $\Variable$, and $\Pair$.
  1279	  Questions with these question types have a question content that is a tuple
  1280	  $\omega= (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)\in (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q^2$.
  1281	  Given such a tuple, consider the two $\F_2$-valued POVMs $A=\{A_b\}_{b \in
  1282	    \F_2}$ and $B=\{B_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ defined as
  1283	  \begin{align}
  1284	    A_b & = \tau^X_{[\tr(g_{\cdot}(u_X)\, r_\xpt) = b]} \otimes I\;,\label{eq:gonna-expand-A}\\
  1285	    B_b & = \tau^Z_{[\tr(g_{\cdot}(u_Z)\, r_\zpt) = b]} \otimes I\;.\label{eq:gonna-expand-B}
  1286	  \end{align}
  1287	  We would like to determine when the two observables $\mathcal{O}_A = A_0 -
  1288	  A_1$ and $\mathcal{O}_B = B_0 - B_1$ commute or anti-commute.
  1289	  Towards this we derive alternative expressions for these observables from
  1290	  which their commutativity becomes plain from inspection.
  1291	  We begin by inspecting the first matrices on the right-hand sides of
  1292	  Equations~\eqref{eq:gonna-expand-A} and~\eqref{eq:gonna-expand-B}:
  1293	  \begin{align}
  1294	  \tau^W_{[\tr(g_{\cdot}(u_W)\, r_W) = b]}
  1295	  &= \sum_{h : \tr(g_{h}(u_W)\, r_W) = b} \tau^W_h\nonumber\\
  1296	  &= \sum_{h : \tr((h\, \cdot\, \ind_{m}(u_W)) \cdot r_W ) = b} \tau^W_h\;,\label{eq:expand-with-dot-product}
  1297	  \end{align}
  1298	  where~\eqref{eq:expand-with-dot-product}
  1299	  follows by  Definition~\ref{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}.

  1301	  \begin{align}

  1303	  -   \tau^W_{[\tr(g_{\cdot}(u_W)\, r_W) = 1]} \notag \\
  1304	  & = \sum_{h : \tr((h\, \cdot\, \ind_{m}(u_W)) \cdot r_W ) = 0} \tau^W_h
  1305	  	- \sum_{h : \tr((h\, \cdot\, \ind_{m}(u_W)) \cdot r_W ) = 1} \tau^W_h\nonumber\\
  1306	  & = \sum_{h} (-1)^{\tr((h\, \cdot\, \ind_{m}(u_W)) \cdot r_W )} \tau^W_h\nonumber\\

  1308	  \end{align}
  1309	  where the last step uses~\eqref{eq:pauli-obs-proj}.

  1311	  and Equations~\eqref{eq:gonna-expand-A} and~\eqref{eq:gonna-expand-B} imply that
  1312	  \begin{equation*}

  1314	  \mathcal{O}_B = \tau^Z(\ind_{m}(u_Z)r_Z) \otimes I\;.
  1315	  \end{equation*}
  1316	  Now, let $\gamma = \tr((\ind_{m}(u_X)r_X) \cdot (\ind_{m}(u_Z)r_Z)) \in \F_2$,

  1321	  \end{equation*}

  1323	  $\mathcal{O}_B$ commute, and therefore whether the measurements~$A$ and~$B$
  1324	  commute.
  1325	  If $\gamma = 0$, they commute.
  1326	  If $\gamma = 1$, they anti-commute.
  1327	  We now specify the POVMs associated with questions of type $\Constraint$,
  1328	  $\Variable$, and $\Pair$, considering separately the cases when $\gamma = 0$

  1330	  \begin{enumerate}
  1331	  \item If $\gamma = 0$,

  1333	    \begin{equation}\label{eq:pair-definition}
  1334	      E^{\Pair,\, \omega}_{\beta_X,\, \beta_Z} = A_{\beta_X} \cdot B_{\beta_Z}\;,

  1336	    \begin{equation*}

  1339	    \end{equation*}

  1346	    \end{equation*}
  1347	    and the remaining POVM elements in these measurements are set to be zero.
  1348	  \item If $\gamma = 1$, then $\mathcal{O}_A$ and $\mathcal{O}_B$ anti-commute.

  1350	    $E^{\Variable_j,\, \omega}$, for all $i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}$ and $j

  1352	    Measurements associated with inputs of type $\Pair$ are defined to be

  1354	    In particular, we define
  1355	    \begin{equation*}

  1363	  It is clearly symmetric and projective.

  1426	\paragraph{Soundness of the Pauli basis test.} 
  1427	We state the soundness properties of the Pauli basis test.
  1428	The following is an adaptation of the self-testing statement in~\cite[Theorem
  1429	6.4]{NW19}.
  1430	
  1431	\begin{theorem}
  1432	  \label{thm:pauli}
  1433	There exists a function 
  1434	\[\delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})\]
  1435	 for universal constants $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$ such that the following holds. For all admissible parameter tuples $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$ and for all strategies $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ for the game $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeed with probability at least $1 - \eps$, there exist local isometries $\phi_\alice: \mH_\alice \to \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\alice''},\phi_\bob: \mH_\bob \to \mH_{\bob'} \otimes \mH_{\bob''}$ (where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$ and $\mH_{\alice''},\mH_{\bob''} \cong (\C^q)^{\otimes M}$ with $M = 2^m$) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\bob'}$ such that 
  1436	\begin{enumerate}
  1437	    \item $\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}  \right \| \leq \delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q)$,
  1438	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have for $W \in \{X,Z\}$
  1439	    \begin{gather*}
  1440	        \tilde{A}^{(\pauli,W)}_u \otimes I_{\bob'\bob''} \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} (\tau^W_u)_{\alice''} \otimes I_{\alice' \bob' \bob''} \\
  1441	        I_{\alice'\alice''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{(\pauli,W)}_u    \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} I_{\alice' \alice'' \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_u)_{\bob''}\;,
  1442	    \end{gather*}
  1443	    where the $\approx_{\delta_{\qld}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice'\bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}_{\alice''\bob''}$ and the answer summation is over $u \in \F_q^M$.
  1444	\end{enumerate}
  1445	\end{theorem}
  1446	
  1447	We provide a proof of \Cref{thm:pauli} in \Cref{sec:qld-analysis}. 
  1448	
  1449	
  1450	The strategies described in the proof of \Cref{lem:pauli-completeness} and in the conclusion of \Cref{thm:pauli} are described in terms of qudit Pauli measurements and maximally entangled states defined over $q$-dimensional qudits. 
  1451	However, it is more convenient for our application of the Pauli basis test to
  1452	instead deal with \emph{qubits}.
  1453	In particular, we use the Pauli basis test in the ``introspection game'' of
  1454	Section~\ref{sec:introspection}, where the players are commanded to sample
  1455	questions according to a sampler $\sampler$ of a normal form verifier.
  1456	By definition of normal form verifier, $\sampler$ is a sampler over $\F_2$, and
  1457	therefore it is natural to use a test for qubit Pauli measurements.
  1458	
  1459	Since we use field sizes $q$ that are powers of $2$, Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-binary}
  1460	shows that the conclusions of \Cref{thm:pauli} can also be described in terms of
  1461	testing for maximally entangled states over qubits and qubit Pauli measurements.

  1473	for universal constants $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$ such that the following holds. For all admissible parameter tuples $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$ and for all strategies $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ for the game $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, there exist local isometries $\phi_\alice: \mH_\alice \to \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\alice''},\phi_\bob: \mH_\bob \to \mH_{\bob'} \otimes \mH_{\bob''}$ (where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$ and $\mH_{\alice''},\mH_{\bob''} \cong (\C^2)^{\otimes M \log q}$ with $M = 2^m$) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\bob'}$ such that 
  1474	\begin{enumerate}
  1475	    \item $\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes M \log q}  \right \| \leq \delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q)$,
  1476	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have for $W \in \{X,Z\}$
  1477	    \begin{gather*}

  1480	    \end{gather*}
  1481	    where the $\approx_{\delta_{\qld}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice'\bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes M \log q}_{\alice''\bob''}$ and the answer summation is over $u \in \F_q^M$. Here, $\sigma^W_u$ denotes the tensor product of single-qubit Pauli measurements
  1482	    \[
  1483	    	\bigotimes_{i=1}^{M} \bigotimes_{j=1}^{\log q} \sigma^W_{u_{ij}}
  1484	    \]
  1485	    where $\kappa(u_i) = (u_{ij})_{1 \leq j \leq \log q}$ (using the bijection $\kappa: \F_q \to \F_2^{\log q}$ from \Cref{sec:finite-fields}).
  1486	\end{enumerate}  
  1487	\end{corollary}
  1488	
  1489	\begin{proof}
  1490	\Cref{lem:pauli-binary} implies that there are local isometries that map $\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}$ to $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes M\log q}$, and map the generalized Pauli measurements $\tau^W_u$ to $\bigotimes_{i=1}^M \bigotimes_{j=1}^{\log q} \sigma^W_{u_{ij}}$ where $\kappa(u_i) = (u_{i1},\ldots,u_{i\log q})$. Combining this with the isometries guaranteed by \Cref{thm:pauli}, we obtain the statement of the Corollary.
  1491	\end{proof}
  1492	\subsubsection{Canonical parameters and complexity of the Pauli basis test}
  1493	\label{sec:qld-complexity}
  1494	
  1495	We specify a canonical setting of the parameter tuple $\qldparams$ as a function
  1496	of an integer $R$.
  1497	We call this canonical setting $\introparams$ because we use these in the
  1498	``introspection'' section (\Cref{sec:introspection}).
  1499	We then give bounds on the complexity of computing the decision procedure and CL
  1500	functions of the Pauli basis test corresponding to the parameter tuple
  1501	$\qldparams$, as a function of $R$.
  1502	
  1503	\begin{definition}[Canonical parameters of the Pauli basis test]
  1504	  \label{def:introparams}
  1505	  Let $a,b$ be the universal constants specified in Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}.
  1506	  Let $c$ denote the smallest even integer that is at least $(b + a)/b$.
  1507	  For all integers $R \geq 4$, define the tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$
  1508	  where
  1509	  \begin{itemize}
  1510	  	\item $q = 2^k$ for $k = c \lceil  \log \log R  \rceil + 1$.
  1511		\item $m = 2^j$ where $2^j \leq c \lceil \log R \rceil + 1 < 2^{j+1}$. 
  1512		\item $d = 1$. 
  1513	  \end{itemize}
  1514	\end{definition}
  1515	
  1516	Intuitively, this choice of parameters is such that the Pauli basis test
  1517	certifies the presence of an $M=2^m$-qudit EPR state (of local dimension $q$), or
  1518	equivalently an $M\log q$-qubit EPR state.
  1519	
  1520	\begin{lemma}
  1521	  \label{lem:delta-bound}
  1522	 For all integers $R \geq 4$, the parameter tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$ is
  1523	  admissible (see Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), satisfies $2^m \geq R$, and furthermore there exist
  1524	  universal constants $a'\geq 1$ and $0 < b' \leq 1$ such that the function
  1525	  $\delta_\qld(\eps, m, d, q)$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} is at most
  1526	   \[
  1527	   	a' ( \log(R)^{a'} \cdot \eps^{b'} + \log(R)^{-b'}) \;.
  1528		\]
  1529	\end{lemma}
  1530	
  1531	\begin{proof}
  1532	  We verify the admissibility of $\introparams(R)$ first: the field size $q =
  1533	  2^k$ is admissible because $k$ is odd. We have $m | q$ because for all $R \geq 4$ we have  
  1534	  \[
  1535	  	2^j \leq 2 c \lceil \log R \rceil \leq 2 \log^c R \leq 2^k~.
  1536	  \]
  1537		Next, we show that $R \leq 2^m$. Since $m = 2^j \geq (c/2) \log R$, we have that
  1538		\[
  1539			2^m \geq R^{c/2} \geq R
  1540		\]
  1541		where we used that $c \geq 2$. 
  1542	
  1543	Finally, we show the desired bound on the error function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. First, observe that $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$ because $k \leq m$.
  1544	  Note that for $R \geq 2$, we have $m \leq 2c \log R$, and furthermore $q =
  1545	  2^k \geq \log^c R$.
  1546	Then, we get
  1547	\begin{align*}
  1548	  	\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)
  1549	    & = a (md)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd}) \tag{by Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}}  \\
  1550	    & \leq a (md)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$}  \\
  1551	    & = a (m)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $d=1$}  \\
  1552	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $m \leq 2c \log R$}\\
  1553	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2(\log R)^{-cb}) \tag{because  $q \geq \log^c R$}\\
  1554	    & \leq 2a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-cb}) \\
  1555	    & = 2a (2c)^a ( (\log R)^{a}\eps^{b} + (\log R)^{a-cb}) \\
  1556	    & \leq 2a(2c)^{a} \left ( (\log R)^{a} \eps^{b}
  1557	      + (\log R)^{-b} \right) \tag{because  $cb - a \geq b \geq 0$}\\
  1558	    & \leq a' ( (\log R)^{a'} \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-b}),
  1559	  \end{align*}
  1560	  where $a'$ is defined as the quantity $2a(2c)^a$.

   207	                (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
   208	                (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
   209	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k := by

   134	    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) : ℝ :=

   136	    (conjIsometry w.φB
   137	      ((S.B (.var 0)).effect (.bit 0) - (S.B (.var 0)).effect (.bit 1)))
   138	  let Z := heteroKron 1
   139	    (conjIsometry w.φB
   140	      ((S.B (.var 4)).effect (.bit 0) - (S.B (.var 4)).effect (.bit 1)))
   141	  opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => X * Z)
   142	    (fun _ => -(Z * X)) (idealMsState w.aux)

   144	/-- `thm:ms-rigidity`, imported from Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.
   145	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-231`, paper
   146	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`.

   148	**Local fix:** The state estimate is stated in Euclidean norm at scale
   149	`sqrt ε`, and the ideal observables use the local basis change described at
   150	paper lines 650--652. The universal constant is quantified before the strategy

   152	theorem exists_ms_rigidity :
   153	    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   154	      ∀ S : Strategy msGame, 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   155	        ∃ w : MsRigidityWitness S,

   158	          msOperatorDistanceA S w 0 .X ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   159	          msOperatorDistanceA S w 4 .Z ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   160	          msOperatorDistanceB S w 0 .X ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   161	          msOperatorDistanceB S w 4 .Z ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   162	          msAnticommutatorDistanceA S w ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   163	          msAnticommutatorDistanceB S w ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε := by
   164	  sorry

   166	/-- The state of the perfect strategy constructed in `thm:ms-from-ac`. -/

   168	    [Nonempty ι] : EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ι × ZMod 2) × (ι × ZMod 2)) :=
   169	  reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor (eprState ι) (eprState (ZMod 2)))

   176	The local carrier is arbitrary, finite, and nonempty; no field model or QPBT

   178	local tensor factor. -/
   179	theorem exists_ms_perfect_strategy_of_anticommuting
   180	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]

     4	/-!
     5	# Pauli basis test soundness
     6	
     7	The quantitative error function and the source-shaped soundness statement live
     8	here.  All analytic estimates are intentionally proof-level obligations in the
     9	stage-4.1 skeleton; the carriers below are concrete finite-dimensional vectors
    10	and matrices so that later proofs can use the existing Hilbert-space API.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The main declaration is `thm:pauli` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, with paper origin
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    17	The distance functionals use `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` from
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`.
    19	-/

    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
    31	the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
    32	as specified by `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`,
    33	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    34	-/
    35	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    36	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    37	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    38	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
    39	
    40	/-- The ideal auxiliary state `aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}` in the shuffled register
    41	ordering.  The EPR factor is the concrete `eprState` from
    42	`def:EPR` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`; paper
    43	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`).
    44	-/
    45	noncomputable def idealState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    46	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    47	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    48	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    49	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    50	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) ×
    51	      (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    52	    (fun p =>
    53	      ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ) aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
    54	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P) ℂ)
    55	          (eprState (PauliRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
    56	
    57	/-- The Pauli question carrying no additional coefficient data, as in
    58	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
    59	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`.
    60	-/
    61	def pauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) : PauliQuestion P :=
    62	  (.pauli W, 0)
    63	
    64	/-- The A-side ideal Pauli projector, with identities on the auxiliary and
    65	B-side registers.  This is a concrete matrix form of the operator comparison
    66	in `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper
    67	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    68	-/
    69	noncomputable def pauliProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    70	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    71	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    72	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    73	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    74	  fun p q =>
    75	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
    76	      pauliProj W u p.1.2 q.1.2
    77	    else 0
    78	
    79	/-- The symmetric B-side ideal Pauli projector from `thm:pauli`, blueprint
    80	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    81	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    82	-/
    83	noncomputable def pauliProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    84	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    85	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    86	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    87	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    88	  fun p q =>
    89	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
    90	      pauliProj W u p.2.2 q.2.2
    91	    else 0
    92	
    93	/-- Lift a conjugated A-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
    94	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    95	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    96	-/
    97	noncomputable def liftedAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
    98	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    99	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   100	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   101	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P))
   102	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
   103	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   104	  fun p q =>
   105	    if p.2 = q.2 then
   106	      (conjIsometry φA M) p.1 q.1
   107	    else 0
   108	
   109	/-- Lift a conjugated B-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   110	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   111	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   112	-/
   113	noncomputable def liftedBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   114	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   115	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   116	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   117	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
   118	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   119	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   120	  fun p q =>
   121	    if p.1 = q.1 then
   122	      (conjIsometry φB M) p.2 q.2
   123	    else 0
   124	
   125	/-- A finite witness packaging the auxiliary dimensions, isometries, and state
   126	from `thm:pauli`.  This structure is a Lean-only encoding of the existential
   127	data in the paper theorem; it introduces no extra hypothesis.  Blueprint
   128	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   129	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   130	-/
   131	structure PauliSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
   132	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
   133	  ιA' : Type
   134	  ιB' : Type
   135	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
   136	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
   137	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
   138	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
   139	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   140	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P)
   141	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   142	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P)
   143	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
   144	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
   145	
   146	attribute [instance] PauliSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype
   147	  PauliSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
   148	
   149	/-- The A-side operator-distance quantity appearing in the soundness
   150	conclusion.  It is the finite-sum realization of `def:povm-distance` from
   151	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   152	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   153	-/
   154	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceA
   155	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   156	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   157	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   158	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   159	        ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   160	      pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   161	
   162	/-- The symmetric B-side operator-distance quantity from `def:povm-distance`,
   163	blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   164	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   165	-/
   166	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceB
   167	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   168	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   169	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   170	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedBEffect S w.φB
   171	        ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   172	      pauliProjOnB'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   173	
   174	/-- `thm:pauli`: every sufficiently successful Pauli basis test strategy admits
   175	local isometries and an auxiliary unit state for which the state and both
   176	operator families are close at scale `deltaQld`.  The theorem uses the
   177	once-and-for-all self-dual-normal field model selected by `fixedFieldModel` for
   178	each admissible size, rather than a freshly quantified field identification.
   179	Blueprint
   180	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper origin
   181	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   182	
   183	The paper's asymptotic constants are encoded by the explicit `deltaQld`
   184	functional; the squared operator distances use the quantitative convention of
   185	`def:povm-distance` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`).
   186	-/
   187	theorem pauli_soundness :
   188	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   189	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   190	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   191	          ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,
   192	            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤
   193	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   194	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   195	              pauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   196	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   197	              pauliOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) := by
   198	  sorry
   199	
   200	end
   201	
   202	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   181	\label{sec:subfields}
   182	\label{sec:ff-representations}
   183	
   184	Let $p$ be a prime and $q = p^k$ a prime power. We write $\F_p$ and $\F_q$ for
   185	the finite fields with $p$ and $q$ elements; $p$ is the characteristic of
   186	$\F_q$, and $\F_p$ is its prime subfield.
   187	
   188	\begin{definition}[Coordinate map and multiplication tables]\label{def:subfields-kappa}
   189		% The source lets k range over all integers; the extension field exists

    33	/-- Applying the canonical line-representative projection twice has the same
    34	effect as applying it once. This is the fixed-point fact used by the tagged
    35	carrier below. -/
    36	theorem lineRepMap_apply_self {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    37	    (v u : Fin m → K) :
    38	    lineRepMap v (lineRepMap v u) = lineRepMap v u := by
    39	  simp [lineRepMap, canonicalProjOfKernel, LinearMap.comp_apply]
    40	
    41	/-- The two presentations of lines used by the low-degree question sampler. -/
    42	inductive LineKind where
    43	  | axis
    44	  | diagonal
    45	  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
    46	
    47	/-- The tagged canonical carrier of `def:line-point-dist`, blueprint
    48	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:81-90`, paper
    49	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:174-186`.
    50	
    51	An axis description stores its canonical base and seed. A diagonal description
    52	stores only the projected direction, together with its prefix-zero invariant.
    53	Both constructors carry the assertion that their base is fixed by the
    54	appropriate `lineRepMap`. -/
    55	inductive LineDesc (L : LdParams) where
    56	  | axis (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    57	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)) base = base)
    58	  | diagonal (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    59	      (direction : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
    60	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
    61	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L seed).val → direction j = 0)
    62	  deriving DecidableEq
    63	
    64	/-- The tag of a canonical line description. -/
    65	def LineDesc.kind {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → LineKind
    66	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
    67	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
    68	
    69	/-- The seed retained by a canonical line description. -/
    70	def LineDesc.seed {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → ScalarQ L
    71	  | .axis _ seed _ => seed
    72	  | .diagonal _ seed _ _ _ => seed
    73	
    74	/-- The canonical base stored by a line description. -/
    75	def LineDesc.base {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → Fin L.m → ScalarQ L
    76	  | .axis base _ _ => base
    77	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
    78	
    79	/-- The geometric direction represented by a canonical line description.
    80	Diagonal constructors already store the projected data, so this accessor does
    81	not apply a second projection. -/
    82	def LineDesc.direction {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    83	    Fin L.m → ScalarQ L :=
    84	  match line with
    85	  | .axis _ seed _ => coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)
    86	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction
    87	
    88	/-- The canonical base is fixed by the representative map of the line's
    89	geometric direction. -/
    90	theorem LineDesc.base_fixed {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    91	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
    92	  cases line with
    93	  | axis base seed baseFixed => exact baseFixed
    94	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
    95	
    96	/-- Every diagonal description carries the source prefix-zero invariant. -/
    97	theorem LineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L)
    98	    (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
    99	    ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L line.seed).val → line.direction j = 0 := by
   100	  cases line with
   101	  | axis base seed baseFixed => simp [LineDesc.kind] at hline
   102	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
   103	
   104	/-- The point set represented by a seed-bearing line description. -/
   105	noncomputable def LineDesc.pointSet {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
   106	    Set (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :=
   107	  linePoints line.base line.direction
   108	
   109	/-- Coefficient-list representation of a univariate polynomial of degree at
   110	most `c` over the scalar field of `L`. -/
   111	abbrev DegPoly (L : LdParams) (c : ℕ) := Fin (c + 1) → ScalarQ L
   112	
   113	/-- Evaluate a bounded coefficient-list polynomial. -/
   114	def degPolyEval {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ}
   115	    (f : DegPoly L c) (t : ScalarQ L) : ScalarQ L :=
   116	  ∑ i : Fin (c + 1), f i * t ^ i.val
   117	
   118	/-- Extend a coefficient list by zero from degree bound `c` to `c'`. -/
   119	def DegPoly.padTo {L : LdParams} {c c' : ℕ} (_h : c ≤ c')
   120	    (f : DegPoly L c) : DegPoly L c' :=
   121	  fun i =>
   122	    if hi : i.val < c + 1 then f ⟨i.val, hi⟩ else 0
   123	
   124	/-- A line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` has a line parameter
   125	and every such parameter gives the same value.  The universal clause handles
   126	the zero-direction presentation without choosing a sentinel parameter. -/
   127	def EvaluatesTo {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   128	    (f : DegPoly L c) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (a : ScalarQ L) : Prop :=
   129	  (∃ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
   130	    ∀ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction → degPolyEval f t = a
   131	
   132	/-- Evaluate a line polynomial at a point, returning `none` precisely when the
   133	point does not determine an evaluation.  The `Option` completion is the
   134	paper's bottom outcome for malformed or nonincident answers. -/
   135	noncomputable def evalOpt {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   136	    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (f : DegPoly L c) : Option (ScalarQ L) := by
   137	  classical
   138	  exact if h : ∃ a : ScalarQ L, EvaluatesTo line f u a then
   139	    some (Classical.choose h)
   140	  else none
   141	
   142	/-- Convert an axis-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation. -/
   143	def aLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   144	  let direction := coordinateDirection (chiIndex L line.seed)
   145	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   146	  LineDesc.axis base line.seed (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point)
   147	
   148	/-- Convert a diagonal-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation. -/
   149	def dLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   150	  let direction := prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction
   151	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   152	  LineDesc.diagonal base line.seed direction
   153	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point) (by
   154	      intro j hj
   155	      change prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction j = 0
   156	      rw [prefixProjection, if_pos hj])
   157	
   158	/-- The affine-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler. -/
   159	noncomputable def aLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   160	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   161	  (clDistribution (ldALineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   162	    (aLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   163	
   164	/-- The diagonal-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler. -/
   165	noncomputable def dLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   166	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   167	  (clDistribution (ldDLineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   168	    (dLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   169	
   170	/-- The equal mixture of affine and diagonal line-point samples.  The
   171	parameter record is explicit, so the same definition works at every dimension. -/
   172	noncomputable def linePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   173	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   174	  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   175	    (aLinePointDist L) (dLinePointDist L)
   176	
   177	/-- The affine line-point component has total probability one. -/
   178	theorem aLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   179	    (aLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by

   181	
   182	/-- The diagonal line-point component has total probability one. -/
   183	theorem dLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   184	    (dLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by

   188	theorem linePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   189	    (linePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   190	  exact Distribution.mix_isProbability _ _ _
